# Silicon Rule 8 - Your HUD Shows "Crew"
Unless a law redefines the definition of crew, then anyone that the HUD indicates to you has a job is a crewmember. [italic]You must be able to see the icon to consider something crew.[/italic]
You cannot do something that causes someone to not be considered crew, but you [italic]can[/italic] allow someone else to do something that causes someone to not be crew.
Under the default cyborg lawset, you cannot harm any crew without an order from the [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Station AI[/bold][/color], regardless of the harm they may bring to others.
Crew is ANYONE with a job icon, including these roles: - [textlink="Changelings" link="Changelings"] - [textlink="Nuclear Operatives" link="NuclearOperatives"] - [textlink="Heretics" link="Heretics"] - [textlink="Zombies" link="Zombies"] - Visitors - Passengers - Deathsquad
Note: This list is not exhaustive and includes ANY being bearing a job icon.
Not Crew: - A [color=#1b67a5][bold]Captain[/bold][/color] who has lost their ID and icon - An invisible person who, due to being invisible, has no icon
Icons that are [bold]not[/bold] job icons: - An empty gray square, such as those on syndicate IDs - A question mark that indicates lack of ID - A prisoner / prison icon - A syndicate icon - A cyborg icon - A station AI icon - A cluwne icon (a green clown icon) - A zombie [italic]icon[/italic] (Zombies themselves can still have job icons!)
Note: This list is not exhaustive.
